data.title: Repeated words
data.solution:
array = input().replace('\\n',' ').split()
n = len(array)
index = 0
words = 0

while index<n-1:
    test = array[index]
    if len(test)==sum([1 for i in test if not i.isalpha()]):
        index+=1
        continue
    count = 0

    for i in range(index+1,n):
        if array[i].lower()!=test.lower():
            break
        count+=1
    if count>0:
        print(test)
        words+=1
        index+=count
    index+=1
if words==0:
    print('No repeats!')
data.statement:
When proofreading, some people have a hard time time seeing repeats, especially if they're broken up onto different lines. The brain just ignores them.

Print all of the consecutively repeated words found in a string, one on each line, to help find such words when editing text.

1) Only one line of input is provided.
2) Words are separated by spaces or line breaks. Line breaks are always represented as {{\n}} (backslash + n) in this clash.
3) Ignore capitalization when comparing.
4) Words that contain non-alphabetic characters will count them as part of the word. E.g. {{it's}}
5) If there are more than two repeated words in a row, output only the first word.
6) When outputting a repeat group, print the first word exactly as it originally appears.
7) Print each repeated word on its own line, in the order found.
8) If there are no repeats, write {{No repeats!}}.

Example:
Input:
Example example text Text text a , a!a. a ,a hi! hi!

Output:
Example
text
hi!

Reasoning:
The first group of repeated words starts with "Example".
The second group of similar words starts with "text".
The third group differs by non-alphabetical characters.
The fourth group of "hi! hi!" is a repeat as every character is the same in each word.
